From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: ops@fastcart.com
Date: 2025-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: [INC-9876] sudden p95 jump on checkout - initial telemetry

Team —

We observed a sharp p95 latency increase impacting the checkout path beginning ~08:58 PST. Key points: 
- Window: 08:58–09:08 PST, sustained p95 from ~420ms -> ~1.8s across gen-api write endpoints.
- Throughput: qps steady but tail latency skewed for requests with >1024 token prompts.
- Error rate: no spike in 5xx but higher client-side timeouts reported by some customers (FastCart included).

I opened INC-9876 and attached a sample CSV snapshot (checkout_latency_snapshot_1118.csv). Initial hypotheses:
1) KV cache evaporation for long-sequence sessions (warmstart misses)
2) a kernel scheduling backlog on a fractional subset of hosts after the 06:30 rollout

Immediate asks:
- SRE/Runtime (karthik) — can you confirm whether recent rollout touched the write cluster and whether warmstart/kvcache metrics show increased miss rate?
- Product (Naomi) / Sales (Jonas) — what level of customer comms do we want now vs. after mitigation? FastCart is already seeing timeouts.
- Please enumerate the tradeoffs cost/latency for the following mitigations: rollback, routing exclusion, aggressive KV warmup. Product needs these called out so PM leadership can approve the path.

Action owners:
- Marissa: continue triage and post kernel/host correlation (INC-9876 link please).
- Karthik: confirm whether we can hotfix or require rollback, and whether we can flip a routing flag to exclude hosts.
- Jonas: draft the customer note and proposed timing for sending (we should avoid alarming language).

Attach any short logs or a one-slide summary to the Jira ticket and link it here. I will loop in Todd if we need SLA/credits signoff.

—Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com

Subject: Re: [INC-9876] sudden p95 jump on checkout - initial telemetry

Naomi / Marissa —

Quick update from runtime side after initial triage:
- Confirmed: rollout at 06:30 modified kernel selection heuristics on the write cluster. On ~12% of hosts we see a kernel scheduling backlog correlated with larger context lengths.
- KV cache: miss rate increased ~3x for sessions with prompt size >1k tokens; warmstart attempts show evictions.

Mitigation options and tradeoffs:
1) Partial rollback of the 06:30 change on affected host subset (~12%): expected to restore p95 within 15–25 minutes but requires a coordinated host-level rollback and brief disruption to that subset (expected <10 minutes per host).
2) Routing exclusion: flip routing flag to avoid the affected hosts — low-risk, immediate, but reduces capacity by ~12% which may increase latency elsewhere under high load.
3) Aggressive KV warmup: deploy a warmup job to prepopulate KV for active sessions — medium effort, takes ~30–45 minutes to see effect, minimal customer disruption.

Recommendation: routing exclusion immediately (safe, reversible), then concurrently start warmup jobs. If routing exclusion causes capacity pressure, plan targeted rollback for hosts with worst backlog.

I attached a tiny patch that enables a temporary routing flag toggle (mitigation_patch.diff) and have added logs to INC-9876. I can flip the flag now if Naomi approves.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Runtime Engineering
